raw_response:
I've been working this land since I was in my twenties. I know Quzhou soil — it's decent loam, responds to fertilizer if you don't overdo it. My well gives me water when the rains don't come, which is most summers. Some of my sons work in Handan now, so during peak times — especially garlic harvest in May — I hire a few day laborers from the village. I can't do everything alone at my age.

My main income is garlic. I plant it in October on 4 mu, let it overwinter, pull it in late May. Then I plant maize on that same 4 mu right after — by mid-June the garlic beds are ready. I keep my remaining 2 mu in wheat because we grind some of it ourselves and I've always grown wheat. My mother grew wheat here. I'm not changing that.

For garlic, I use the white variety I've grown for years — I save the best cloves myself. I don't trust new varieties from salespeople I don't know. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and urea when the leaves start shooting up in spring. Garlic needs water consistently during bulb swell — I run the pump six times from autumn through late spring. I spray three times for purple blotch and rust, which hit us badly two years ago.

For maize, I buy hybrid seed from the village supply co-op — I've used the same variety for 8 years, it yields reliably. I fertilize at planting and topdress when the plant is knee-high. Three irrigations: before tassel, at silking, and grain fill. Two pesticide rounds for borer and leaf blight.

For wheat, I use an improved semi-dwarf variety I get from the county seed station. I rotate in a little more phosphorus here because the soil on that 2 mu strip tends to run lean. Four irrigations including the winter freeze-protection water in December. Two spray rounds for powdery mildew and aphids.

I'm not experimenting this year. I need the income steady.
